What I read and the order: AGENTS.md (from context), docs/REVISION-AND-REVIEWS.md, docs/NARRATIVE-FLOW.md and docs/PROMPTS.md. Then, using Read, I opened and looked at storyboards-unnumbered/page-03.png and the composed review/page-03.png. Only after that did I read the full request JSON, source/original.txt, storyboards/page-03.png, and review/page-02.png and review/page-04.png for the page boundaries. All files were readable. I did not open the SVGs or the cast reference sheets.

03-1 to 03-2 reverse angle: this reads clearly in the composed art. In 03-1 Meera is in the left foreground behind the desk, seen over her shoulder, and Ravi is at the glass door on the right. In 03-2 the left foreground holds Ravi's green shirt, the edge of his beard and dark hair, his bag strap and his hand on the phone. Meera faces the camera behind the same cream counter with the black monitor and keyboard, and her blue kurta and braid match 03-1. The over-the-shoulder framing and the matching costumes make the camera flip readable. It does not look like the characters swapped places. From 03-2 onward Ravi stays left and Meera right in 03-3 and 03-4, so the axis holds after the reset.
The 03-3 desk top is now cream. It matches the counter in 03-1 and 03-2 and the desk in 03-4, so the wide two-shot reads as the same desk.

The first reader's points against the art: (1) The side swap is now carried by the over-shoulder reverse described above. (2) Registration is now shown: in 03-3 Meera types and the monitor is turned toward the front with blank fields, so 'Yes, please.' -> 'You're all set' does not skip the action. (3) 'today's appointment' is verbatim source text and reads as 'today's visit'. It is acceptable. (5) Place and time are now set by the reception counter, monitor, waiting chairs with seated patients, glass entrance, daylight and 'Good morning'.

Panel sizes and roles: 03-1 is a large arrival panel and 03-2 a narrow consent question. 03-3 is the widest panel and holds the registration action, not just two words. 03-4 is the short close-out with Meera's gesture toward the chairs. There is one balloon per panel, each sits near its speaker's face and each tail points to that speaker. The tail in 03-4 runs from the balloon down-right to Meera.

Not blocking, for the artwork reviewers: in 03-2 the waiting chairs with patients appear behind Meera, but in 03-1 and 03-4 they are on the patient side. The room layout is therefore slightly inconsistent, though readers recognise the space from the characters and desk, so reading is not affected. A navy phone lies beside Meera's keyboard in 03-1 (the recorded reception-mobile), and Ravi holds a similar navy phone in 03-2. A careless reader could think he picked up the reception phone. Page 5 makes clear that he has his own phone. The prop record lists them as separate phones.

On the unnumbered placeholder page and the composed page, I read in this order: 'Good morning! I'd like to see the doctor.' (top-left balloon, tail right to Ravi waving at the door), then 'Of course. May I register your details...' (top right, tail down to Meera), then 'Yes, please.' (middle, top left, tail to Ravi nodding), then 'You're all set, Ravi. Please have a seat.' (bottom, tail to Meera gesturing). This matches the intended order and the numbered storyboard.

No two balloons that are out of sequence sit close together: each panel has one balloon. In 03-4 the balloon sits between Ravi's face and Meera's, and it is still read as Meera's because the tail is clear and her hand gesture points toward the seats behind Ravi.
In the composed art Ravi's reaction to the consent question can be read. In 03-3 he nods with eyes closed while Meera types, then in 03-4 he turns toward the chairs.

transitions.observation: Page 02 ends in the evening office: sunset windows in 02-1 and 02-2, Ananya and Meera with laptop and staff phone. 03-1 opens on bright daylight at a reception counter, with a new character waving in at a glass door and saying 'Good morning'. The change of time and place reads from light, setting and greeting without a caption. The tidy desk with its monitor ties back to the onboarding.

This is the intended reverse over-the-shoulder cut, and it reads clearly. In 03-1 Meera is in the left foreground and Ravi at the door. In 03-2 Ravi's green shirt, beard edge and bag strap are in the left foreground and Meera faces us behind the same cream counter and black monitor. The matching costumes and desk carry the flip. Meera's 'Of course' answers his request directly.

Same counter and the same left/right placement: Ravi left, Meera right. The wide two-shot shows him agreeing with 'Yes, please.' while she types and turns the monitor toward him with blank fields. That directly answers the consent question and shows the registration step. His phone moves from his hand to the desk.

Same staging and same cream desk. Registration is finished: Meera says 'You're all set, Ravi' and gestures toward the waiting chairs behind Ravi at the left, and he turns with his hand on his bag strap. Cause and effect are continuous.

'Please have a seat' and the waiting chairs lead to 04-1: a doctor's room with a white-coated Ananya at a desk with a window and plant, and Ravi just sitting down with his bag on the floor. The wait is skipped, but the move to the consultation reads from the setting change and his unchanged costume. Ananya greets him by name, which links back to the registration.

readingReview.comparison: The first reading (placeholder ネーム) found an unexplained side swap, registration that was never shown, an unclear 'today's appointment', and no place or time cue. The composed art now answers the side swap with a legible over-shoulder reverse in 03-2 and keeps the axis through 03-4. It shows registration in 03-3 (typing, monitor with blank fields, cream desk matching the counter) and sets reception and morning visually. 'today's appointment' is verbatim source text and is acceptable. The dialogue order is unchanged from the first reading, which already read it as intended. Only non-blocking art notes remain: the position of the waiting chairs in 03-2, and the reception phone looking like Ravi's phone.

What I read and the order: with Read I opened and looked at storyboards-unnumbered/page-04.png and review/page-04.png before the request JSON. I then read the full request, source/original.txt and storyboards/page-04.png, plus review/page-03.png and review/page-05.png for the page boundaries. All files were readable.

Missing reaction beat around 04-3 (first reader's point a): in the composed art, 04-3 is itself the reaction. Ananya faces Ravi, whose back of head and green shoulder are in the right foreground. She leans in slightly with her hands folded and a soft, concerned smile, and small nod marks sit beside her head. Read after Ravi's 'I've been feeling tired lately', this works as a silent listening acknowledgement. 04-4 'We'll go through your concerns...' then answers his complaint directly. The source says panel 3 is 'The doctor listens with attention' and forbids diagnosis and medical advice. Adding a spoken question or acknowledgement risks clinical content, so a silent attentive face is the appropriate beat. I do not think a further dialogue beat is required.

What 'technology' refers to: the rectangular box is the same narrator caption style as page 02's 'The clinic begins its Welbuk onboarding.', so its voice is clear as narration. 'Technology' points back to the Welbuk systems set up on pages 02-03 (laptop setup, staff phone, reception monitor). On this page the visual support is the closed laptop pushed aside on the doctor's desk, clearly visible in 04-1 at the left edge and in 04-4. In 04-3 itself the closed laptop is only a small grey sliver at the bottom-left corner, so the caption gets little support inside its own panel. It still reads as intended from the page and from the comic so far. The caption is verbatim source text. Not blocking: if the panel is ever repainted, making the closed laptop slightly more legible in 04-3 would strengthen the 'in the background' contrast.

First reader's points (b) and (c), the clipped labels and the missing face boxes in 04-2 and 04-3, belong to the placeholder ネーム. In the art, Ananya's back of head appears in 04-2 and Ravi's in 04-3, and the request records them as kind 'head' at the frame edge, so both are present without being face-visible speakers. Ananya keeps left and Ravi right across all four panels.

Point (d), the panel sizes: 04-1 is large because it establishes the new room, both people and the closed laptop. Ravi's complaint in 04-2 and the reaction in 04-3 share the middle row at equal size, which pairs statement and response. The page stays calm and unhurried, matching its stated purpose. Nothing on the page reads as diagnosis, prescription or an instrument in use: the stethoscope is only worn.

Reading order on the composed page: 'Hello, Ravi. Tell me what brings you in.' (top, tail left to Ananya), then 'I've been feeling tired lately.' (middle-left, tail to Ravi rubbing his neck), then the caption 'Technology supports the workflow. The conversation stays human.' (middle right, over Ananya listening), then 'We'll go through your concerns and decide the right next steps together.' (bottom, tail to Ananya). This matches the intended order.

Each panel has one text element, so nothing can be read ahead out of order. After reading the caption in 04-3, the eye goes to Ananya's listening face before dropping to 04-4. Her reaction to Ravi's complaint is therefore read before her reply.

transitions.observation: From the reception, where Meera says 'Please have a seat', to the consultation room: a white-coated doctor at a desk with a window and plant, and Ravi in the same green shirt sitting down with his bag on the floor. The change of place and the same visit read from setting and costume. 'Hello, Ravi' follows from the registration.

Ananya asks what brings him in. In 04-2 the camera is from her side, with her back of head in the left foreground, and Ravi answers that he has been tired while rubbing his neck. The question and answer are adjacent and the left/right placement is kept.

Reverse view from Ravi's side, with his back of head and green shoulder at right and Ananya facing right. She leans in with folded hands and nod marks: this is the silent listening reaction to his complaint. The caption supplies the thematic narration over this beat. The left/right placement matches 04-1.

Back to the two-shot: Ananya, after listening, now speaks with an open hand, and Ravi nods, relaxed, with his bag beside the chair. 'Your concerns' refers back to his tiredness in 04-2. No treatment advice is given.

From the consultation room to the same reception from page 03: Meera's blue kurta and braid, the black monitor, the blue waiting chairs with patients. Ravi now has his bag back on his shoulder and holds his phone. There is no caption, but the familiar reception and the bag back on his shoulder show that this is after the consultation.

readingReview.comparison: The first reading (placeholder ネーム) asked for a reaction beat after 'tired lately', for the caption's voice to be clarified and for 'technology' to be explained, and for the visible faces in 04-2 and 04-3 to be defined. In the composed art, 04-3 shows Ananya's attentive, nodding reaction, which supplies the missing beat without adding dialogue that could become medical advice. The narrator style makes the caption's voice clear. 'Technology' is supported by the Welbuk devices on pages 02-03 and the closed laptop pushed aside in 04-1 and 04-4. Its support inside 04-3 is weak (only a sliver of the laptop), but this does not block reading. The backs of heads now define both people in 04-2 and 04-3. The dialogue order is the same as in the first reading.

What I read and the order: with Read I opened and looked at storyboards-unnumbered/page-05.png and review/page-05.png before the request JSON. I then read the full request, source/original.txt and storyboards/page-05.png, plus review/page-04.png and review/page-06.png for the page boundaries. All files were readable. On the numbered storyboard only, the teal label in 05-2 overlaps the guide caption '2 / Ravi sees a conceptual app screen'. That text is a guide annotation and does not appear on the composed page.

First reader's point 1, no time or place cue: in the art, 05-1 is clearly the page-03 reception, with Meera, the black monitor, the plant, and the blue waiting chairs with seated patients. Ravi has his bag on his shoulder again, so the scene reads as back at reception after the consultation.

First reader's point 2, the logical step behind 'So': 05-2 shows the phone screen facing the reader with calendar and heart cards, and Ravi looks up thoughtfully. His 'So I can keep useful information in one place?' reads as an inference from what he sees on the screen, not only from Meera's words. In 05-1 Meera points at the phone, which sets this up. The step is no longer skipped.

In 05-2 Ravi glances up to screen-right, away from Meera, who is off-panel left. This is recorded as a deliberate thinking look. In the art it reads as musing, and Meera's reply in 05-3, where she faces right toward Ravi's back and his phone, closes the exchange. This does not block reading.

Left/right note: on page 05 Meera is left and Ravi right, the reverse of 03-2 to 03-4 but the same as 03-1. This follows a page turn and a scene change, and the desk and monitor make the space recognisable, so it does not confuse. The placement is kept within page 05.

05-4 makes the source's 'Ravi leaves, reassured' readable: an exterior street view, Ravi waving back, and Ananya and Meera waving from the glass doorway. The caption is verbatim source narration in the narrator style. It reads as a summary rather than story dialogue, which is consistent with the comic's promotional framing. The walkthrough offered in 05-3 happens between panels and is not shown. That is acceptable, because the caption summarises the visit.

Reading order on the composed page: 'Welbuk Health is designed to help patients stay connected with their care.' (top-left balloon, tail right to Meera pointing at the phone), then 'So I can keep useful information in one place?' (middle-left top, tail to Ravi), then the teal label 'WELBUK HEALTH for patients' (bottom left of 05-2, beside the phone screen), then 'That's the idea. Let's walk through what is available to you.' (middle right, tail down to Meera), then the caption 'A smoother visit. A more connected experience.' (bottom panel, top). This matches the intended order.

In 05-2 the label sits low, near the phone screen, so it is read after the question and works as a product tag. The eye then rises to the 05-3 balloon at the top of the same row, which is a normal row-to-row reading path. Meera's line is not read before Ravi's question.

transitions.observation: From the consultation room, which ends with 'decide the right next steps together', back to the familiar page-03 reception: Meera, the monitor, the waiting chairs. Ravi has his bag back on his shoulder and holds his own phone. The setting and the bag show this is after the consultation and on his way out.

Meera points at Ravi's phone. In 05-2 we see the screen, with calendar and heart cards, as he holds it with both hands and asks whether it keeps information in one place. Seeing the screen connects her explanation to his inference. The reception monitor and plant in the left foreground keep the place.

Meera answers 'That's the idea' facing right toward Ravi, whose back and phone are in the right foreground. This keeps 05-1's placement of Meera left and Ravi right, and the answer directly follows his question.

After Meera's offer of a walkthrough, the view cuts outside: Ravi steps onto the street, waving back, with his bag on and phone in hand, and Ananya and Meera wave from the glass doorway. The cut reads as the end of the visit, and the caption sums it up.

From waving goodbye at the clinic to Ravi at a train window with a moving city skyline, under the caption 'Tomorrow, care may take us beyond our hometown.' The caption and the train set the conditional time jump. The same shirt, bag and phone keep him recognisable. Page 06 then moves into the clearly labelled WELBUK VISION vignettes.

readingReview.comparison: The first reading (placeholder ネーム) found no time or place cue after page 04, a logical step skipped behind 'So', and an unclear final panel. The composed art resolves these: 05-1 is visibly the same reception with Ravi on his way out, the app screen in 05-2 supports his inference, and 05-4 clearly shows him leaving with both staff waving. The dialogue and label order matches the first reading and the intended order. The ad-like tone of the caption is verbatim source text and does not block reading.
